$comment: EXP-1490 (eMCP E1, epic VAPP-175, 2026-10-31): WHO SEES WHICH APP TOOL. ONE ENDPOINT, `/api/mcp/apps`, ONE OAUTH FLOW: the consent page picks ONE team, the apps (all, or a list) and Read only | Full, and connects missing upstreams inline (upstream.json). THE GRANT MODEL: `mcp_grants` (one row per user × OAuth client × kind; the unique key becomes (user_id, client_id, kind)) gains `kind` (`grantKinds`: `builtin` = the existing `/api/mcp` grant over teams/boards, every existing row; `apps` = a `/api/mcp/apps` grant), `all_apps` (boolean, default false), `app_ids` (jsonb string[], default []) and `access` (`grantAccess`: `read` | `full`, default `full`). An `apps` grant names exactly one team in `team_ids` (`all_teams` false), no boards, and EITHER `all_apps` OR a non-empty `app_ids` (never both); a `builtin` grant has no apps and access `full` (`grantErrors` → the reasons, `grantCases`; a malformed row grants nothing). `all_apps` covers apps created later; `app_ids` naming a trashed or deleted app simply stops matching it. THE ACCESS RULE (`effectiveAccess`, `accessCases`): levels `none` < `read` < `write`; effective access to an app = the grant (`read` → read, `full` → write) ∩ the member's policy for that app ∩ (per tool) the tool's level. The member's POLICY is the Settings › MCP Access table (member × app, set by owners): no row = `write` (`policyCases`). Access is `none` for an app outside the grant (another team, not listed), a trashed app, a caller who is no longer a member of the grant's team, a grant of kind `builtin` or a malformed grant. A tool is VISIBLE (listed in tools/list) and CALLABLE iff the effective level ≥ its `access` (`visibleCases`): a read token never sees a write tool, and a call to a tool not listed answers MCP's unknown-tool error, never a hint that it exists. Destructive tools never exist (exposes.json). REVOCATION CASCADES: deleting the grant (Settings › MCP Clients, or the member leaving the team) or the OAuth client deletes its access and refresh tokens in the same transaction; trashing an app drops its tools on the next tools/list (the broker sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` to live sessions); removing an upstream server deletes every member's credential for it (the existing `mcp_credentials` cascade) and its bindings answer `upstreamMissing` (upstream.json).
